name: Jiajun Wu

research_topics: neuro-symbolic concept learning and program-structured representations
multi-modal perception from visual, acoustic, and tactile signals

current_direction: Benchmarking spatial belief and embodied cognition in foundation models
Neuro-symbolic / program-structured concepts as the abstraction layer
Training-free compositional control of diffusion generation

current_direction_basis: Drawn from the 2026 and 2025 entries on his own publications page (https://jiajunwu.com/#publications), fetched 2026-08-31. 4D/world generation: WonderZoom, PerpetualWonder, NEUROK, and Choreographing a World of Dynamic Objects (all CVPR 2026), continuing WonderPlay and WorldScore (ICCV 2025). Spatial/embodied cognition benchmarks: Spatial Mental Modeling from Limited Views, ENACT, and Theory of Space (all ICLR 2026). Neuro-symbolic: Building Intelligent Agents with Neuro-Symbolic Concepts (CACM 2026) and Neuro-Symbolic Decoding of Neural Activity (ICLR 2026), plus From Programs to Poses (NeurIPS 2025). Compositional diffusion control: Product of Experts for Visual Generation (ICLR 2026) and Coupled Diffusion Sampling for Training-Free Multi-View Image Editing (CVPR 2026). Robotics: DexSkin and BEHAVIOR Robot Suite (CoRL 2025), TWIST2 (ICRA 2026), MoMaGen (ICLR 2026). NOT based on the older biography paragraph on the same page.

recruiting.statement: Thank you for your interest in joining my group! Due to the large number of emails I receive, I cannot respond to every email individually. Please review the information below before contacting me. Thanks. Current Stanford students and prospective visiting students: please fill out this form. For Stanford MS students and undergraduates, the minimum time commitment is 15 hours per week for six months. For visiting graduate students, the minimum length of a visit is six months. Prospective postdocs: please email me directly with your CV. Prospective graduate students: please apply through the system and list me as a potential advisor in your application. There is no need to contact me, unless you have a particular research question/idea that you would like to discuss further.

state_rationale:
UPHELD on a second, independent adversarial fact-check (2026-08-31, curl + browser UA, fetched fresh rather than trusting the prior pass). https://jiajunwu.com/ returned HTTP 200 (1,243,212 bytes) and the recruiting block was read directly out of the served HTML source (div class="recruit" id="recruit", raw lines 147-158), so it is server-rendered and not injected by JavaScript. It contains verbatim, in the present tense, an instruction that names undergraduates explicitly: "Current Stanford students and prospective visiting students: please fill out this form. For Stanford MS students and undergraduates, the minimum time commitment is 15 hours per week for six months." This clears the OPENING bar on both required tests. (a) Present-tense open: 'please fill out this form' is a live imperative intake instruction, and a full-page scan for negative recruiting language ('not taking', 'not accepting', 'no longer', 'unable to take') returned ZERO matches. (b) Undergraduate-specific, not PhD-only: undergraduates are named by name and given their own concrete requirement, and the PhD channel is a physically separate paragraph ('Prospective graduate students: please apply through the system and list me as a potential advisor'), as is the postdoc channel. So this is not a case of a grad-admissions notice being misread as an undergraduate opening. NEW EVIDENCE this pass, which the prior review did not have: the server returns 'last-modified: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 03:32:05 GMT' - the page carrying this recruiting text was updated 14 days before today (2026-08-31). That directly answers the main threat to an OPENING claim, which is stale text left up for years, and is why confidence rises 0.70 -> 0.75. REMAINING AND UNRESOLVED CAVEAT, stated plainly: the Google Form is the only action channel an undergraduate has, and it could NOT be opened. It returns HTTP 401 behind a Google sign-in/cookie wall ('You must sign in to access this content'). Critically, that 401 is Google's DEFAULT response to any unauthenticated fetch of any Form, open or closed, so it is not evidence the form is shut - but it is also not evidence it is live. Whether the form is still accepting responses is genuinely unknown, and confidence is capped at 0.75 for that reason alone. Secondary caveat: the group roster publishes Postdocs, PhD Students, Affiliates and Alumni with no undergraduate heading, so the pathway is documented but its throughput is unproven.
